stops.title: St Bride's, Fleet Street
stops.where: Fleet Street, at the top of Bride Lane
stops.directions: Fleet Street, at the top of Bride Lane. Cross to the north pavement so you can see the whole spire at once.
stops.look:
Step back until you can see the whole spire.

Count the tiers. Each one is smaller than the one below it. Four of them, and then a point.

Now think of a wedding cake.
stops.after:
The story goes that a baker on Ludgate Hill called William Rich could see this spire from his shop, and built a cake in its shape for his own wedding.

Nobody has ever proved it. But the shape is the shape, and every tiered wedding cake since is a copy of a church steeple you have walked past a hundred times without looking up.

Wren gave every one of his churches a different spire, and he did it on purpose. From street level you hardly saw the building at all. What you saw was the spire, over the rooftops, from three streets away. So that is where he put the work.

This one is the tallest he ever built.
